title: Sanierung Mehrfamilienhaus - Kopernikusring 1-9, 36-44 16227 Eberswalde, Deutschland, Fassadenarbeiten
description: Das Bauvorhaben umfasst die Sanierung und Modernisierung der bestehenden Mehrfamilienhäuser. Die Gebäude stammen aus dem Jahr 1973 und umfassen insgesamt ca. 180 Wohneinheiten mit einer Gesamtwohnfläche von ca. 10.967 m². Der Wohnungsbestand ist überwiegend vermietet; eine Teilsanierung erfolgte im Jahr 1994. Weitere Leerwohnungsinstandsetzungen finden seit dem Jahr 2025 statt und sind bei der Abstimmung der Schnittstellen zu berücksichtigen. Die zu vergebenden Leistungen betreffen die Instandsetzung und malermäßige Überarbeitung der bestehenden Fassaden einschließlich der zugehörigen Untergrundvorbereitungs-, Schutz-, Anschluss- und Nebenarbeiten. Die vorhandenen Außenwände bestehen gemäß Modernisierungskonzept aus ca. 29 cm Leichtbeton und einem bestehenden Wärmedämmverbundsystem mit ca. 8 cm EPS-Dämmung einschließlich Armierungsschicht und Oberputz. Das vorhandene Wärmedämmverbundsystem soll grundsätzlich erhalten und in schadhaften Bereichen örtlich instand gesetzt bzw. teilweise erneuert werden. Eine vollflächige Erneuerung oder Aufdopplung der Fassadendämmung ist im Modernisierungskonzept nicht vorgesehen. Die Arbeiten erfolgen überwiegend im bewohnten Bestand. Der Schutz der Bewohner, die Nutzbarkeit der erforderlichen Gebäudezugänge sowie der Schutz vorhandener und bereits erneuerter Bauteile sind zu berücksichtigen. Fördervorbehalt BEG EM, aufschiebende Bedingung Die ausgeschriebenen Leistungen sind Gegenstand einer beantragten Förderung nach BEG EM. Der Vertrag wird mit Zuschlag geschlossen; die Lieferungs- und Leistungspflichten stehen unter der aufschiebenden Bedingung der Förderzusage. Sie werden erst und nur insoweit wirksam, wie die beantragte Förderung durch die zuständige Förderstelle bewilligt wird. Der Auftraggeber informiert den Auftragnehmer über den Eintritt der Bedingung unverzüglich in Textform. Bis dahin bestehen keine Ausführungs-, Beschaffungs-, Vorhalte- oder sonstigen kostenverursachenden Leistungspflichten des Auftragnehmers. Wird die Förderung abgelehnt oder tritt die Bedingung nicht bis zum 01.03.2027 ein, entfällt die Verpflichtung zur Ausführung der betroffenen Leistungen. Ausführungsfristen beginnen erst mit Eintritt der Bedingung; weitergehende Ansprüche wegen des Nichteintritts sind ausgeschlossen.

title: Purchase of two (2) Millimetre-Wave Frequency Extender Modules for a Vector Network Analyzers (VNAs) from 110 GHz to 170 GHz
description: NRC Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics (HAA) requires extended measurement capabilities in the millimetre-wave frequency range to support ongoing research in characterizing front-end components for low-noise receivers in radio astronomy. Existing Vector Network Analyzers (VNAs) at NRC HAA are currently limited to a maximum operational frequency of 116 GHz. To increase its measurement capability, NRC HAA intends to acquire frequency extender modules covering the 110–170 GHz band. These extenders must integrate with either of HAA's existing analysers (Keysight PNA N5227B and Rohde & Schwarz ZNA67), providing high dynamic range and stable two-port measurements.

title: W8703-290119- Request for Proposal Littoral UAS
description: ATTENTION: All required supporting documentation and bid submission must be submitted by 25 November 2026 14:00 EST. The Defence Investment Agency, on behalf of the Department of National Defence, is seeking offers from qualified Stream 1 Supply Arrangement holders under the Defence Drone Initiative for the acquisition of a Littoral Uncrewed Aircraft System (UAS) capability. The requirement supports domestic operations conducted by the Canadian Army, including intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance activities, situational awareness, force protection, disaster response, search and rescue support, infrastructure assessment, training, and experimentation. The procurement includes the supply and delivery of a minimum of eighty (80) UAS systems, associated payloads, ground control stations, support equipment, technical publications, spare parts, software and firmware support, and train-the-trainer services. The requirement also includes airworthiness support, cybersecurity assurance, supply chain security, spectrum supportability, configuration management, and lifecycle sustainment requirements.

title: Ireland – Construction work – 14 Tullyglass Hill
description: Corlann Clare invites tenders from suitably experienced building contractors for the extension and refurbishment of an existing single-storey dwelling at 14 Tullyglass Hill, Shannon, Co. Clare, V14 KH42. The works comprise a new single-storey extension of approximately 45 m² and the full refurbishment and upgrade of the existing house. The main elements are: • Demolition and strip-out: demolition of the existing lean-to structure on the east side; removal of the glazed courtyard roof, chimney stack, oil boiler and oil tank; full internal strip-out of finishes, ceilings, fittings, sanitaryware, and heating, plumbing and electrical installations. • New extension: 225 mm solid blockwork on a raft foundation to the Structural Engineer's design, with a certified external wall insulation and render system, and an insulated warm-deck flat roof. • Existing house: replacement of all windows and external doors; new and altered openings with steel beams and lintels; removal and alteration of internal walls; upgrade of all existing flat roofs to warm-deck construction; a new solid warm-deck roof with rooflights over the courtyard; rebuilt rooflight upstand walls; render repairs and redecoration; new fascias, gutters and downpipes. • Internal fit-out: new internal layout including WC and shower rooms, a widened stair and a new platform lift; FD30 fire door sets with closers and electromagnetic hold-open devices; fire-rated glazing; automatic opening smoke vents linked to a fire alarm system; [new heating, ventilation and electrical installations to the Specification]. • External works: widened entrance and tarmac driveway; new gently sloped footpaths and a level landing at a relocated main entrance on the west elevation; new and rebuilt retaining walls; new patio; replacement of asewer lines, installation of new manholes; new surface water drainage; tree removal and reinstatement of landscaping.

title: U006--VR&E Self-Employment Services RFI
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) SUBJECT Exploring the Feasibility of VA Partnering with Industry to Ready Disabled Veterans for Self-Employment (i.e., entrepreneurship; small business ownership) 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA), is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) for Veteran Readiness & Employment (VR&E) Self-Employment Services. The information provided in response to this request may be used by VBA in developing its acquisition strategy and refining the Performance Work Statement (PWS). THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this RFI or otherwise pay for the information requested. Responses will be treated as information only and not as a proposal. There is no obligation for the Government to acquire any products or services described in this RFI. In accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) Subpart 15.101(c)(2), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. 2.0 BACKGROUND VBA s VR&E Service, pursuant to Title 38 United States Code Chapter 31 (see Section 3100), provides to eligible Veterans with compensable service-connected disabilities all services and assistance necessary to enable them to achieve maximum independence in daily living and, to the maximum extent feasible, to become employable and to obtain and maintain suitable employment. After achieving the degree of rehabilitation needed to become suitably employed, VR&E is expected to assist Veterans in the pursuit of suitable employment. One such avenue through which VR&E assists is utilizing VR&E s Self-Employment Track, which is intended to assist eligible Veterans in achieving their vocational goals in entrepreneurship and business ownership. Services include the following: Developing and strengthening a business plan Training in small-business operations, marketing, finances, etc. Assessing the feasibility of implementing such a business plan Obtaining (through loans or grants) the resources necessary to implement a business plan and incorporate the business such as securing loans Purchasing of equipment, acquiring initial stocks and supplies, etc. Specialized expertise and/or support to assist Veterans interested in self-employment includes, but is not limited to, knowledge of local/state/federal laws associated with starting a business;� market research/analysis both from the perspective of assessing viability of the prospective business in the job market and through the lens of purchasing subject matter expertise and purchasing equipment/supplies; and� potential screening or other assessment tools for specialized job markets (i.e. ability to run background checks and/or credit checks to assess criminal history, driving records, substance use/abuse, financial/credit/tax history, education, etc.). Further, VA recognizes that achieving successful self-employment outcomes often requires specialized expertise beyond traditional vocational rehabilitation services. Veterans pursuing entrepreneurship may need support with business planning, feasibility analysis, market research, financial literacy, regulatory compliance, business startup requirements, mentorship, and access to entrepreneurial networks and resources. Self-employment cases frequently involve complex business considerations that require specialized knowledge, individualized assessments, and coordination with public and private sector resources. Veterans may require assistance evaluating business viability, developing comprehensive business plans, understanding applicable licensing and regulatory requirements, conducting market and financial analyses, identifying startup resource needs, and building the skills necessary to successfully operate a small business. These needs often require tailored, ongoing guidance throughout the planning and launch process. VA is seeking information on how experienced industry partners can supplement existing VR&E services by providing subject matter expertise, structured entrepreneurial training, business feasibility assessments, market research capabilities, business financial planning and analysis (i.e., financial projections, startup cost estimates, cash flow planning, and capital requirements), and access to established business support networks. Such services may help Veterans make informed business decisions, evaluate and strengthen the viability of proposed business ventures, develop stronger business plans, and access the expertise and resources needed to successfully launch and sustain a small business. Accordingly, VA requests information from organizations with demonstrated experience providing entrepreneur and small business support services, including business advisory services, training, business feasibility and market assessments, entrepreneurial training, startup incubation, financial planning, and other related support services. The goal is to identify potential partnership approaches that can enhance VA's ability to assist Veterans with service-connected disabilities in evaluating business concepts, developing viable business plans, preparing for business ownership, and successfully launching and sustaining small businesses 3.0 INFORMATION SOUGHT The Government is seeking the following information from vendors responding to this RFI: Organization and Contact Information, specifically: Name of Organization Addresses for Primary Locations of Operation Points of Contact (available for follow-up discussions) Phone Numbers and Email Addresses for Points of Contact Business Size and Socioeconomic Status Answers to List of Questions (See Section 5.0 of this RFI) Past Performance (if applicable) describing how your organization: has supported entrepreneurs in exploring, planning, and starting small business enterprises prepared entrepreneurs for operating small business enterprises with training, apprenticeships, mentorships, and similar educational ventures 4.0 SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Please submit responses to the Contracting Officer, Edward Bradford, via email Edward.Bradford@va.gov no later than November 25, 2026. Responses shall not exceed 10 pages total and shall be prepared in Times New Roman, 12-point font, with 1-inch margins. 5.0 LIST OF QUESTIONS Please provide information regarding proposed joint ventures, teaming arrangements, or strategic alliances you believe would be beneficial in supporting the needs of Veterans pursuing self-employment outlined in the background section of this document. Please describe your organization s expertise in providing business planning, self-employment, entrepreneurship, small business operations, and startup incubation services. Please describe how your organization would prepare for and respond to referrals issued by VR&E, specifically the timelines for contacting Veterans participating in the Self-Employment Track and the type of services your organization would provide throughout the engagement. Please describe your organization s service delivery model, including how services would be documented and how progress, milestones, and outcomes would be communicated to VA. On average, how many full-time equivalent (FTE) business consultants, entrepreneurship specialists, or small business advisors are employed by your company? How long has your company been providing self-employment, entrepreneurship development, small business consulting, or related business advisory services? Please provide the qualifications, certifications, or specialized training your business consultants possess related to entrepreneurship? Please describe your experience developing business plans, feasibility studies, and financial projections. title: Cell Window Glazing
description: Cell Window Glazing This requirement is for: The Correctional Service of Canada, Kent Institution, Pacific Region. Trade agreement: Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA). Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: Barring any other conditions or international sanctions, Canadian Suppliers, Suppliers of an Applicable Trading Partner and Suppliers of a Non-Trading Partner, are eligible for this solicitation. Competitive Procurement Strategy: lowest priced compliant bid. Set-aside under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business: This procurement is not subject to any set-asides for Indigenous Suppliers. Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement: This procurement is not subject to a Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement. Security Requirements: This contract does not include security requirements. Nature of Requirements: The following is a summary of the statement of work for this requirement. The Correctional Service Canada has a requirement to replace the existing cell window glazing and installation of the polycarbonate security screens to prevent inmates from manipulating window assemblies and receiving contraband delivered by drone. Objectives: To improve the integrity and security of cell windows by installing enhanced glazing and security measures that prevent inmates from damaging, manipulating, removing, or otherwise compromising window assemblies to receive contraband. Deliverables: The Contractor shall: • Supply and install new security glazing in 168 windows located within POD 1 and POD 2, for a total of 504 glazing panels. • Supply and install one polycarbonate security screen on each of the 168 windows in accordance with the construction drawings. • Supply and install all required security screws, fasteners, and accessories identified in the construction drawings and specifications. • Apply security caulking to all newly installed glazing assemblies. • Apply security caulking to the 12 existing windows located in L-Range, POD 1. • Ensure all work is completed in accordance with the construction drawings, specifications, manufacturer’s instructions, and institutional security requirements. Any conditions for participation of suppliers not specified in solicitation documentation: none. Estimated quantity of commodity: see solicitation document statement of work and basis of payment. Duration of Contract and Time Frame for Delivery: Construction Time: The Contractor must perform and complete the Work within forty-four (44) weeks from the date of notification of acceptance of the offer. title: APN-CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT SERVICES, MAINLAND BC INFRASTRUCTURE MODERNIZATION
description: ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT SERVICES FOR MAINLAND BRITISH COLUMBIA INFRASTRUCTURE MODERNIZATION PROGRAM (with security requirements) 1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at Chilliwack, British Columbia and various range and training areas across Mainland BC. The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). 2. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT AND SERVICES It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND. APN: 87908 Approximate Estimate: $125,000,000 Anticipated Posting: Winter 2027 Description: The Infrastructure Modernization Program at Chilliwack, British Columbia and various range and training areas across Mainland BC is focused on both recapitalization of existing assets and the development of new infrastructure and facilities where required. As part of this project, the Department of National Defence (DND) wishes to proceed with the renewal of systems which include civil, architectural, mechanical, electrical, and environmental elements to bring the assets to meet current and projected future requirements. This program will include planned phased work packages for implementation over ten (10) years while maintaining operations across Mainland BC. The purpose of this project is to retain the services of a contractor to provide construction management services of pre-construction and construction phases.  Major construction services are expected to include activities such as interior/exterior demolition in the presence of hazardous materials, interior renovations, exterior envelope work, electrical, mechanical, civil, structural and new infrastructure. 3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS To be eligible for contract award, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS). 4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN. 5. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a contractor: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation being advertised on MERX, has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package prior to the closing date indicated in the solicitation, and has submitted a proposal.   DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Note – Contractors that do not submit a proposal will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process. Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. 6. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Theresa Tran Coordinator, Contract Services Defence Construction Canada (604) 832 8373 theresa.tran@dcc-cdc.gc.ca 7. Disclaimer DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations  or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the proponent agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

title: Request for Information (RFI) � Market Research for Ocean Transportation of Hazardous Waste (Guam to CONUS)
description: *** Please be advised that this RFI - Market Research is posted under both NAICS codes 483113 and 483111 to ensure the broadest possible industry dissemination. The postings are identical; interested parties need submit only one response. *** November 3, 2026 Attention Maritime Transportation / Ocean Freight industry partners: Request for Information (RFI) � Market Research for Ocean Transportation of Hazardous Waste (Guam to CONUS) The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) is conducting a market survey to determine the commercial availability and operational capacity of ocean carriers to transport government-generated hazardous waste from the Territory of Guam to permitted facilities in the United States. Pursuant to the Military Cargo Preference Act (10 U.S.C. � 2631) and coastwise trade statutes under 46 U.S.C. Chapter 551, the Government is evaluating the availability of qualified U.S.-flagged vessels, including coastwise-endorsed vessels and U.S.-flagged vessels operating under registry endorsements in accordance with the statutory Guam trade exemption (46 U.S.C. � 12111(b)). This market survey assesses industry capability to meet technical environmental safety standards and required volume throughput, while establishing factual market data regarding whether domestic vessel capacity is sufficient or if alternative statutory authorities, such as the hazardous waste transport exception under 46 U.S.C. � 55105(b) or applicable administrative waiver procedures must be evaluated to ensure mission readiness and regulatory compliance. 1. The current Cargo Description and Operational Requirements for DLA are: a. Cargo Type: Department of War (DoW) Generated Hazardous Waste. The waste streams include a broad range of materials, including: i. RCRA-regulated hazardous waste: Waste exhibiting ignitability (D001), corrosivity (D002), reactivity (D003), or toxicity characteristics, including waste containing lead, chromium, cadmium, mercury, benzene, and other hazardous constituents. ii. Contaminated liquids: Waste fuels, gasoline, solvents, paints, thinners, corrosive liquids, contaminated wastewater, and other petroleum- or chemically contaminated liquids. iii. Used oil and petroleum-related waste: Used lubricating oil, oily water, oil filters, sludge, and petroleum contaminated materials, some of which may be managed as non-RCRA-regulated waste. iv. Batteries: Lithium-ion batteries, lithium-metal batteries, lead-acid batteries, nickel-cadmium batteries, and other spent batteries requiring regulated transportation or disposal. v. Contaminated solids: Paint debris, spent blasting media, contaminated soil, oily rags, absorbents, filters, and other solids contaminated with hazardous substances. vi. Other hazardous materials and waste: Oxidizers, corrosive chemicals, flammable substances, aerosol waste, and compressed gas cylinders, where applicable. The cargo includes both RCRA hazardous waste requiring a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest and other regulated or non-hazardous waste streams. Individual shipments vary in composition and may contain materials classified under multiple DOT/IMDG hazard classes, including Classes 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, and 9. b. Waste is generally packaged in approved drums, intermediate bulk containers (IBCs), or other appropriate containers and consolidated into 40-foot shipping containers. Bulk liquid waste may also be transported in ISO tank containers. The applicable waste classifications, quantities, and packaging are identified on the corresponding waste profiles, manifests, and shipping documents. c. Hazard Class/UN Number Required: (See Attached List.) d. Required Weekly Throughput Estimate: 2 Each � (40-Foot Container�s) e. Route: Guam to United States (West Coast) f. Required Shipping Window: Present � Indefinite Interested industry partners are requested to submit a written response to this Request for Information (RFI) within twenty (20) calendar days from the date of publication of this notice. This will enable the Government to thoroughly evaluate commercial market capacity, operational feasibility, and statutory compliance. Submissions should directly address the following required questions: 1. Company Information a. Company Legal Name: b. Company Cage Code: c. Physical Address: d. Website: e. Primary NAICS code: f. Business Size (large / small): g. Any socioeconomic status, if any: 2. Point of Contact a. Name: b. Title: c. Phone: d. Email: 3. Status: Does your company currently operate a Jones Act-compliant vessel scheduled on this route during the specified shipping window? 4. Technical Certification: Is your company legally certified and operationally equipped to accept, stow, and transport all the specific classes of hazardous waste listed? (See attached �DLA-GUAM � Hazardous Waste List�.) 5. Volume and Throughput Capacity? (Critical): 6. What is the maximum volume (measured in standard Conex/ISO container equivalents) that your company can commit to transporting on this route per week for the DoW, and DoW Contractors for the Hazard Class/UN Number Required? 7. Can your company meet or exceed the military's minimum required throughput of 2 Each � 40-Foot Container�s (or equivalent) without causing operational or regulatory storage backlogs in Guam? 8. If your company can only offer partial or restricted capacity (e.g., limiting transport to 1 container per week/voyage), please provide specific operational, regulatory, or safety constraints dictating this volume limit. Commercial Intent: If your company possesses both the technical capability and the required volume capacity, is your company willing to support the DoW, and DoW Contractors executing the removal of hazardous waste from Guam? Justification for Refusal: If your company is unable or unwilling to accept this cargo, or cannot meet the required weekly volume throughput, please state the specific technical, regulatory, safety, or vessel allocation reasons for your refusal/capacity limitation. This RFI-Market Research does not constitute a solicitation and does not obligate the Government to issue a solicitation, award a contract, or pay for information submitted in response to this notice. The Government will utilize the provided data, as well as any omissions, to assess commercial capability, capacity, availability, procurement strategies, and hazardous waste transportation exceptions. Please submit your written response directly to Bradley Moehlig at Bradley.Moehlig@dla.mil & Mike Mamaty at Michael.Mamaty@dla.mil . Submissions should be delivered electronically via email in Adobe PDF or Microsoft Word format. Please referencing Subject Line: 'Response to RFI � Maritime Transport of Hazardous Waste (Guam to CONUS)'. description: *** Please be advised that this RFI - Market Research is posted under both NAICS codes 483113 and 483111 to ensure the broadest possible industry dissemination. The postings are identical; interested parties need submit only one response. *** November 3, 2026 Attention Maritime Transportation / Ocean Freight industry partners: Request for Information (RFI) � Market Research for Ocean Transportation of Hazardous Waste (Guam to CONUS) The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) is conducting a market survey to determine the commercial availability and operational capacity of ocean carriers to transport government-generated hazardous waste from the Territory of Guam to permitted facilities in the United States. Pursuant to the Military Cargo Preference Act (10 U.S.C. � 2631) and coastwise trade statutes under 46 U.S.C. Chapter 551, the Government is evaluating the availability of qualified U.S.-flagged vessels, including coastwise-endorsed vessels and U.S.-flagged vessels operating under registry endorsements in accordance with the statutory Guam trade exemption (46 U.S.C. � 12111(b)). This market survey assesses industry capability to meet technical environmental safety standards and required volume throughput, while establishing factual market data regarding whether domestic vessel capacity is sufficient or if alternative statutory authorities, such as the hazardous waste transport exception under 46 U.S.C. � 55105(b) or applicable administrative waiver procedures must be evaluated to ensure mission readiness and regulatory compliance. 1. The current Cargo Description and Operational Requirements for DLA are: a. Cargo Type: Department of War (DoW) Generated Hazardous Waste. The waste streams include a broad range of materials, including: i. RCRA-regulated hazardous waste: Waste exhibiting ignitability (D001), corrosivity (D002), reactivity (D003), or toxicity characteristics, including waste containing lead, chromium, cadmium, mercury, benzene, and other hazardous constituents. ii. Contaminated liquids: Waste fuels, gasoline, solvents, paints, thinners, corrosive liquids, contaminated wastewater, and other petroleum- or chemically contaminated liquids. iii. Used oil and petroleum-related waste: Used lubricating oil, oily water, oil filters, sludge, and petroleum contaminated materials, some of which may be managed as non-RCRA-regulated waste. iv. Batteries: Lithium-ion batteries, lithium-metal batteries, lead-acid batteries, nickel-cadmium batteries, and other spent batteries requiring regulated transportation or disposal. v. Contaminated solids: Paint debris, spent blasting media, contaminated soil, oily rags, absorbents, filters, and other solids contaminated with hazardous substances. vi. Other hazardous materials and waste: Oxidizers, corrosive chemicals, flammable substances, aerosol waste, and compressed gas cylinders, where applicable. The cargo includes both RCRA hazardous waste requiring a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest and other regulated or non-hazardous waste streams. Individual shipments vary in composition and may contain materials classified under multiple DOT/IMDG hazard classes, including Classes 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, and 9. b. Waste is generally packaged in approved drums, intermediate bulk containers (IBCs), or other appropriate containers and consolidated into 40-foot shipping containers. Bulk liquid waste may also be transported in ISO tank containers. The applicable waste classifications, quantities, and packaging are identified on the corresponding waste profiles, manifests, and shipping documents. c. Hazard Class/UN Number Required: (See Attached List.) d. Required Weekly Throughput Estimate: 2 Each � (40-Foot Container�s) e. Route: Guam to United States (West Coast) f. Required Shipping Window: Present � Indefinite Interested industry partners are requested to submit a written response to this Request for Information (RFI) within twenty (20) calendar days from the date of publication of this notice. This will enable the Government to thoroughly evaluate commercial market capacity, operational feasibility, and statutory compliance. Submissions should directly address the following required questions: 1. Company Information a. Company Legal Name: b. Company Cage Code: c. Physical Address: d. Website: e. Primary NAICS code: f. Business Size (large / small): g. Any socioeconomic status, if any: 2. Point of Contact a. Name: b. Title: c. Phone: d. Email: 3. Status: Does your company currently operate a Jones Act-compliant vessel scheduled on this route during the specified shipping window? 4. Technical Certification: Is your company legally certified and operationally equipped to accept, stow, and transport all the specific classes of hazardous waste listed? (See attached �DLA-GUAM � Hazardous Waste List�.) 5. Volume and Throughput Capacity? (Critical): 6. What is the maximum volume (measured in standard Conex/ISO container equivalents) that your company can commit to transporting on this route per week for the DoW, and DoW Contractors for the Hazard Class/UN Number Required? 7. Can your company meet or exceed the military's minimum required throughput of 2 Each � 40-Foot Container�s (or equivalent) without causing operational or regulatory storage backlogs in Guam? 8. If your company can only offer partial or restricted capacity (e.g., limiting transport to 1 container per week/voyage), please provide specific operational, regulatory, or safety constraints dictating this volume limit. Commercial Intent: If your company possesses both the technical capability and the required volume capacity, is your company willing to support the DoW, and DoW Contractors executing the removal of hazardous waste from Guam? Justification for Refusal: If your company is unable or unwilling to accept this cargo, or cannot meet the required weekly volume throughput, please state the specific technical, regulatory, safety, or vessel allocation reasons for your refusal/capacity limitation. This RFI-Market Research does not constitute a solicitation and does not obligate the Government to issue a solicitation, award a contract, or pay for information submitted in response to this notice. The Government will utilize the provided data, as well as any omissions, to assess commercial capability, capacity, availability, procurement strategies, and hazardous waste transportation exceptions. Please submit your written response directly to Bradley Moehlig at Bradley.Moehlig@dla.mil & Mike Mamaty at Michael.Mamaty@dla.mil . Submissions should be delivered electronically via email in Adobe PDF or Microsoft Word format. Please referencing Subject Line: 'Response to RFI � Maritime Transport of Hazardous Waste (Guam to CONUS)'. Timely submission of capabilities, vessel availability, and commercial operating constraints will directly inform DLA's acquisition strategy, small business determinations, and required statutory compliance determinations under federal maritime law.

title: NAWCAD HX-21 CH-53K ORGANIZATIONAL LEVEL CONTRACTOR MAINTENANCE SUPPORT (CMS)
description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION a. The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD), Naval Test Wing Atlantic (NTWL), Air Test and Evaluation Squadron TWO ONE (HX-21), Patuxent River, MD, has a follow-on requirement for Contractor Maintenance Support (CMS) Services to perform Organizational Level (O-Level) maintenance support services on assigned CH-53K test aircraft. This Market Research tool is being used to identify potential and eligible firms, of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. The results of the Sources Sought will be utilized to determine if any Small Business Set[1]Aside opportunities exist. Additionally, this Sources Sought is being used to gather constructive information from industry to improve the Request for Proposal (RFP). This is for the NAWCAD HX-21 CH-53K O-LEVEL CMS. This is a follow-on requirement. The current contract information can be found in Section 3.0, paragraph b below. There have been significant changes to the scope as follows: estimated on-site personnel increasing from 62 FTEs to 75 FTEs. This is not subject to bundling or consolidation. b. The following documents are attached to this Sources Sought Notice: Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) Draft Labor Categories and Staffing Matrix Draft Personnel Qualifications c. The following dates are anticipated time frames associated with this requirement: Estimated Draft RFP Release: 01 May 2027 Estimated Final RFP Release: 01 Aug 2027 Estimated Award Date: 01 May 2028 Period of Performance: 19 Aug 2028 � 18 Aug 2033 d. Primary Work Location/Place of Performance: Primary Work Location is detailed in Attachment 1, Draft PWS. 2.0 DISCLAIMER THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. 3.0 ANTICIPATED CONTRACT TYPE AND CONTRACT/PROGRAM BACKGROUND a. Anticipated Contract Type: C-Type Contract with Firm Fixed Price (FFP) CLINs for Labor and Cost Reimbursable CLINs for associated Other Direct Costs (ODCs). The Government is anticipating an additional Cost Reimbursable Performance Incentive CLIN. The anticipated Period of Performance includes one base period of 12 months with four one[1]year option periods for a total potential performance period of 5 years. b. The incumbent contract information is as follows: Incumbent Contractor: Adams Communication & Engineering Technology, Inc. Contract Number: N68520-20-D-0032 / N00421-23-F-0619 Contract End Date: 13 Aug 2028 Contract Type: FFP Previous Set-Aside Designation: Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB) Number of FTEs on the Contract: 62 FTEs c. Program Background: HX-21 has a follow-on requirement for CMS Services to perform O-Level (to include limited Intermediate Level (I-Level) and Depot Level (D[1]Level)) maintenance support services and other explicit test support tasks required to maintain assigned CH-53K aircraft to the proper standards required to meet the requirements of the HX-21 test schedule. The test schedule includes both flight and ground test events to meet the PMA-261 and other requirement owner program performance needs. The limited I-Level and D-Level work is contingent, provided skilled artisans and required tools are available and authorization is received from the cognizant authority. Services include aircraft maintenance and logistics support on aircraft, aircraft systems, and Support Equipment (SE) for which HX-21 has cognizant responsibility. Additional services include maintenance of prototype aircraft components, configuration and installation of internal/external ballast, and Helicopter Support Team (HST) duties, i.e. external sling load operations. The majority of work performance will be accomplished at Patuxent River, Maryland. Additional temporary work sites in direct support of projects are executed as detachments and include (but are not limited to) United States Naval Vessels, Department of War Installations, and Commercial Facilities which also encompass unscheduled emergent type maintenance support. A more detailed description is provided in Attachment 1, Draft PWS. 4.0 SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS AND REQUIRED CAPABILITES Any anticipated special requirements and required capabilities are detailed in Attachment 1, Draft PWS. This document details security clearance requirements for personnel, facility requirements, and any specific certifications that are required for the performance of this requirement. 5.0 ELIGIBILITY a. The applicable NAICS code for this requirement is 488190, Other Support Activities for Air Transportation, with a Small Business Size Standard of $40.0M. b. The Product Service Code is J015, Maintenance, Repair, and Rebuilding of Equipment: Aircraft and Airframe Structural Components. c. Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement. Note: FAR 52.219-14 Limitation on Subcontracting requires a small business prime on a Set-Aside to perform at least 50% of the cost of contract performance. Small business primes may now count �first tier subcontracted� work performed by similarly situated entities as if it were performed by the prime itself. Please read the full text of the clause deviation (52.219-14 Class Deviation 2020-O0008 dated 04/03/20 at https://www.acquisition.gov/browse/index/far). To assist in our market research and determination of any applicable small business set-aside for this effort, if you are a small business interested in priming this effort and plan to utilize �similarly situated entities� to meet the Limitations on Subcontracting, please identify the name & CAGE Code of the specific firm(s) you intend to partner/subcontract with to meet the requirements as well as their SB size status under the NAICS that you as the prime would assign for their workshare. Information regarding any planned similarly situated entity should be included in answering any questions outlined in the Sources Sought Notice (SSN) in order to assist the Government�s capability determination. 6.0 SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS a. The responses to these questions will aid the Government in determining whether a company is capable in performing the requirement, so it is important to address these areas with specific details. Organizational-Level Maintenance on Navy/Marine Corps Rotary Wing Aircraft. List all type/model rotary wing aircraft supported and total number of each within the past five years. Describe all experience with ground and flight operations to include launch/recovery of rotary wing aircraft and hot pressure refueling. List all type/model aircraft and locations / supported organization. Safe for Flight (SFF) experience. State any experience with loading / rigging of internal and external slung cargo. Maintenance Training. State any experience with training a maintenance workforce on a new aircraft. L

title: Trenching, Conduit and Ground-well Installation
description: Description The United Stated Embassy in Kingston is requesting proposals for Trenching, Conduit And Ground-Well Installation in various locations on the Embassy compound. The contractor will provide all labor, equipment, supervision, material specific to the back filling and compaction and management needed to complete the job Infrastructure Support System - Handhole / Underground Conduit System Trenching Nine locations have been identified requiring trench work. Thirteen locations have been identified requiring trench work. Before excavation, the Contractor shall locate and verify all existing utilities in the proposed trench alignment. If excavation interferes with existing drains, piping, or structures, the Contractor shall immediately notify, in writing, the COR and provide temporary protection for these systems before proceeding. Trenching from Handholes The Contractor shall make wall penetrations into existing manholes/handholes as required for the number and size of conduits entering and exiting each structure, in accordance with the drawings. Conduit Existing conduit shall remain in place unless the drawings specifically direct removal or modification. Under grass, soil, the Contractor shall install Schedule 80 PVC conduit with a minimum cover of 24 inches (610 mm) from finished grade to top of conduit, or as indicated on the drawings, whichever is greater. All underground 90 degree bends with a 12inch (305 mm) radius shall use prefabricated sweeping bends. Above grade, all underground PVC conduit shall transition to rigid galvanized steel (RGS) using PVC to RGS couplers. The Contractor shall install pull lines in all new conduit runs. Soil and Backfill Materials Soil Materials The Contractor shall provide all labor and materials for soil and backfill, where required. Select Backfill: ASTM D 2487 soil classification groups SW, SP, and SM, or combinations thereof; free of rock or gravel larger than 3 inches (75 mm), debris, waste, frozen materials, vegetation, and other deleterious matter. Asphalt/Concrete Base Course: Naturally or artificially graded mixture of natural or crushed gravel, crushed stone, and natural or crushed sand; ASTM D 2940; with at least 95% passing a 11/2inch (40 mm) sieve and not more than 8% passing a 1/4inch (6.4 mm) sieve. Base Gravel: Naturally or artificially graded mixture of natural or crushed gravel, crushed stone, and natural or crushed sand; ASTM D 2940; 100% passing a 1inch (25 mm) sieve and not more than 8% passing a 1/4inch (6.4 mm) sieve. Sand Cushion: ASTM C 33 fine aggregate, natural or manufactured sand. Placement and Compaction Place backfill and fill in layers not exceeding: 8 inches (203 mm) loose thickness for heavy compaction equipment; 4 inches (102 mm) loose thickness when compacted by hand-operated tampers. Place backfill and fill evenly to the required elevations, uniformly along their full length. Compact soil materials to not less than the following percentages of maximum dry unit weight per ASTM D 1557: Under lawns or unpaved areas: scarify and re-compact top 6 inches (152 mm) below subgrade and compact each layer to 85%. Utility trenches: compact each layer of initial and final backfill to 85%. Anticipated Period of Performance: a base period of twenty-one (21) days after contract award Eligibility and Registration Offerors must hold an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) when they submit a proposal and at award. To ensure access you are required to be approved prior to the visit. You are to provide the full names of the attendees, the vehicle information to include make, model, color and plate number of the vehicle being driven. The email must be sent no later than Wednesday, November 04, 2026 by 2 pm. Completed proposal are to be email to kingstonquotes@state.gov in PDF format by the deadline stipulated.

title: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Marshalling Services - Yuma, AZ
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Marshalling Services 1.0 Description The General Services Administration (GSA) Office of Fleet Management (GSA Fleet) has a requirement to acquire contractor support for vehicle auction and marshalling services or marshalling only services for Government vehicles. Services are required on or about January 1, 2027 � December 31, 2030 in Yuma, AZ. Interested parties must be located within 50 miles of the Yuma, AZ area. The vendor must be the owner or legal lessee of the facility. Auction and marshalling site tasks include, but are not limited to: Advise the government on optimal disposition strategy for individual exchange/sale-eligible vehicles worldwide to maximize public participation and net proceeds, to include strategies for specialty (law enforcement, buses, ambulances, medium & heavy trucks, etc.) as well as Zero Emission Vehicles to include battery electric vehicles, plug-in hybrid vehicles and/or fuel cell vehicles. Perform full vehicle inspections and ensure complete condition reporting, imagery capture (including high-definition photo and video, 360� views, etc.), and accurate description writing. Provide recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Create and execute marketing plans/campaigns to catalog vehicles and announce vehicle sales to the public as required by law, and to advertise to/connect with the broadest possible market audience. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles and vehicle-related assets (e.g., license plates, removed equipment, telematics devices). Support the creation and management of all required vehicle disposition documentation/records. Conduct activities related to bidder/buyer management, including registration, validation/eligibility checks, etc. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to bidders/buyers throughout the sales process to ensure a seamless, transparent, and customer-centric buying experience. Facilitate and perform payment collection process. Encourage maximum participation by offering a range of non-government affiliated services (retail financing, aftermarket warranties, vehicle enhancement etc.). Store, service and remarket of electric vehicles to include any necessary charging infrastructure. Transport vehicles to and from vendor locations. Prepare vehicles for public inspection and final sales/disposition, including services such as reconditioning, maintenance and repair, as well as equipment removal/disposal, and license plate & government credit card disposal and tracking. Offer industry-aligned services for customers to perform vehicle test drives. Provide state-of-the-art technology that will improve customer experience including enhanced condition reporting, 360� views, video, high-definition photography, etc. Conduct a full and open competitive sales process, including public inspection periods for all vehicles, and any related sale services for exchange/sale property. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage, and release of vehicles from time of receipt until final removal. Manage the logistics of vehicle transportation to bring vehicles to sale. Prepare vehicles for sale, to include vehicle equipment removal/disposal, reconditioning, and repairs. Work with local government entities to facilitate any inspections, documentation, and any other actions required to complete transactions in local markets. Perform electronic inventory management, vehicle inspection, complete condition reporting for vehicles. Offer recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, local market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Provide customer service to buyers in global markets. Create and execute marketing campaigns for local markets. Offer an internet sales platform with the potential to reach a global audience. Collect proceeds from vehicle sales and if necessary, convert to U.S. dollars. Marshalling only site tasks include, but are not limited to: Transport or resource/transportation of vehicles to and from vendor location (e.g., customer location, OEM dealership, offsite repair facility). Inspect vehicles upon delivery for various factors including but not limited to any damage to the vehicle, all components of the vehicle are accounted for (e.g., keys, floor mats, etc.), and missing equipment. Perform telematics device installation and/or activation on all new vehicles prior to releasing the vehicle to the customer. Validate new vehicles and options to vehicle order information provided by GSA. Perform pre-delivery inspections (PDI) in accordance with the manufacturer�s standards. Prepare new vehicles for customer receipt. Provide driver education for customers including vehicle operation, unique features, infotainment settings, etc. Offer specialized expertise and support on Electric Vehicle management, operation and charging infrastructure. Charge battery-powered vehicles. Maintain all vehicle fuel and charge levels as prescribed in the Statement of Work by GSA. Perform custodial and sales preparation services to facilitate auction house sales of GSA exchange lease vehicles. Process and manage all required vehicle shipment and delivery documentation. Manage scheduled vehicle appointments and ensure accurate vehicle exchanges. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Kansas City District is issuing a solicitation for an Integrated Design and Construction (IDaC) services delivery method contract for the construction of a new bed tower, clinical expansion, parking garage in support of the Veterans Affairs St. Louis Health Care System (VASTLHCS) John Cochran (JC) Hospital in St. Louis, Missouri. title: Pilot Training Transformation Device Support Services IV (PTT DSS IV)
description: The purpose of this requirement is to maintain and support PTT device solutions based on state- of-the-art commercial simulation environments, hardware solutions for the cockpit simulation environment, and ancillary software elements.The Contractor shall provide all services and equipment necessary to install, maintain, and support new and existing PTT devices. Devices currently fit into the following classifications: common Immersive Training Device (cITD), enhanced Immersive Training Devices (eITD), and Helicopter Immersive Training Device (HITD). Any new classifications will need to be defined and evaluated prior to inclusion in this scope. The Contractor shall support 142 ITDs and up to 17 Instructor Operating Stations (IOS) at the following locations: Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA) Randolph, TX; Columbus Air Force Base (AFB), MS; Laughlin AFB, TX; Vance AFB, OK, Sheppard AFB, TX; and Fort Rucker, AL. The Government has the right to modify the quantity of devices/locations pending contract modification and funding. The Contractor shall maintain a common software interface to integrate current and future PTT software and hardware components as required by program goals, hardware solutions for the cockpit simulation environment, and on-premises network and data architecture hardware and support, as appropriate for deployed training systems.

description: The purpose of this requirement is to maintain and support PTT device solutions based on state- of-the-art commercial simulation environments, hardware solutions for the cockpit simulation environment, and ancillary software elements.The Contractor shall provide all services and equipment necessary to install, maintain, and support new and existing PTT devices. Devices currently fit into the following classifications: common Immersive Training Device (cITD), enhanced Immersive Training Devices (eITD), and Helicopter Immersive Training Device (HITD). Any new classifications will need to be defined and evaluated prior to inclusion in this scope. The Contractor shall support 142 ITDs and up to 17 Instructor Operating Stations (IOS) at the following locations: Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA) Randolph, TX; Columbus Air Force Base (AFB), MS; Laughlin AFB, TX; Vance AFB, OK, Sheppard AFB, TX; and Fort Rucker, AL. The Government has the right to modify the quantity of devices/locations pending contract modification and funding. The Contractor shall maintain a common software interface to integrate current and future PTT software and hardware components as required by program goals, hardware solutions for the cockpit simulation environment, and on-premises network and data architecture hardware and support, as appropriate for deployed training systems.

title: France – Road transport services – 26SERV12 - Accord cadre à bons de commande pour les prestations de transport d'oeuvres et objets d'art pour les besoins de la Métropole Toulon Provence Méditerranée
description: Dans le cadre de sa politique culturelle, la Métropole Toulon Provence Méditerranée poursuit une politique d'attractivité territoriale en vue d'assurer un développement dynamique et durable et assume à ce titre la gestion en régie directe d'équipements culturels dans le domaine des arts visuels qui contribuent à son rayonnement au niveau national et international et dispose d'une collection d'oeuvres et objets d'art (art contemporain, photographie, sculptures). La présente consultation porte sur les besoins de la Métropole Toulon Provence Méditerranée en matière de prestations de transport d'oeuvres et objets d'art et activités connexes. Ces besoins concernent les oeuvres et objets d'art empruntés ou prêtés en France ou à l'étranger auprès d'acteurs publics et/ou privés (musées, institutions culturelles, galeries, collectionneurs...) pour la réalisation d'expositions temporaires ou dans le cadre de mouvements d'oeuvres. Ces prestations comprennent : - l'emballage des oeuvres et objets d'art avec étiquetage (du simple tamponnage à la fabrication et à la mise en caisse) aller/retour ; - les formalités « Beaux-arts » et douanières, - le transport des oeuvres et objets d'art par tout moyen (transport routier, aérien, maritime, fluvial ferroviaire) : l'acheminement depuis le ou les lieux d'enlèvement désignés (en France ou à l'étranger) vers les lieux de livraison désignés (en France ou à l'étranger) - les manutentions et le bardage (à savoir toutes formes de manutention manuelle ou mécanique pour déplacer et installer les oeuvres et objets d'art) à l'aller (avec une possible répartition dans les espaces des lieux désignés) et au retour, - le déballage des oeuvres et objets d'art à l'aller et au retour, - l'entreposage des oeuvres et objets d'art - des prestations complémentaires - le suivi et la coordination de ces différentes opérations.

title: Request for Information (RFI) for Aerial Targets Branch (EBAY) Air Force Aerial Target Solutions
description: Issued pursuant to Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) FAR 15.101(c) and RFO FAR Part 10 solely for information, market research, and planning purposes. This market survey is conducted by the Aerial Targets Program Office (AFLCMC/EBAY) under the Air Force Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Weapons (AFPAE/WP) to obtain industry capabilities, rough order of magnitude (ROM) information, and data needed to support commercial product/service, non-developmental item (NDI), and small business determinations under RFO FAR 10.001(f), and to inform acquisition planning. Per Title 10, U.S. Code �4172, major munitions and missile programs must demonstrate lethality against appropriate, threat-representative targets prior to full-rate production. The Aerial Targets mission is to provide target aircraft that replicate threat systems, including performance, signatures, and countermeasures of adversary aircraft. The objective of this RFI is to identify a range of solutions to populate a family for systems needed throughout the spectrum of missions in Defensive and Offensive Counter Air capabilities. These solutions may represent the full range of airborne threats, spanning from inexpensive �hobby drones� to the most advance adversary fighter and large-scale aircraft. This RFI is intended to: Identify commercially available or near-term solutions Understand industry capabilities and innovative approaches Inform future acquisition strategies and budgetary requirements and assist the agency in making commerciality, NDI, and small business set-aside determinations See attached RFI and Question and Answer documents and for additional details. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ In accordance with Section 10 of the attached RFI, attached are the final Questions and Answers posted on 11 SEPTEMBER 2026. ALL FINAL RESPONSES ARE DUE BY 28 SEPTEMBER 2026 @ 1600 CENTRAL.

title: Sources Sought for Co-Brand Agreement for Door Hardware
description: On behalf of the U.S. AbilityOne Commission (Commission) the independent federal agency that administers the AbilityOne Program, (National Industries for the Blind (NIB), a designated central nonprofit agency, is pursuing potential partnerships with U.S. commercial manufacturers of Door Hardware for the purpose of providing employment for people who are blind or severely disabled. If successful, the result will be the addition of the product(s) to the AbilityOne Procurement List (PL) under a co-brand agreement between the manufacturer and the AbilityOne Program, and its registered brands. The (Door Hardware) must meet and/or exceed FAR and other Federal Government published standards, Executive Orders and Federal Agency requirements. At a minimum, the following criteria must be met: PRODUCT Meet and/or exceed FAR and other Federal Government published standards, Executive Orders and Federal Agency requirements. The product must meet industry performance specifications and standards for construction, performance, sustainability and reliability. Be manufactured and lab tested, certified and customer tested to be effective according to their purpose, have current Material Safety Data sheets if necessary, and meet certifications with corresponding documentation designated by customers. Meet industry performance specifications and standards for construction, performance, sustainability and reliability. MANUFACTURER Must possess a nationally or industry-known brand name that can demonstrate significant appeal through evidence of substantial sales. Willing to allow NPA employees to work at their facility. Demonstrate how it will assist the Commission�s designated nonprofit agency (NPA) to expand its line of Door Hardware, thus increasing blind work hours, while keeping expansion costs to the NPA at a minimum. Willing to deliver bulk materials to the non-profit agency to assure the agency of on-time deliveries to federal government customer(s). Willing to enter into a multi-year agreement to include: On-going technical and production assistance. The necessary factory trained technical field support Enabling the non-profit agency to meet the criteria of the AbilityOne Program to convert material, fill containers, label, assemble and package the products thereby creating employment for people who are blind or severely disabled. Demonstrate a commitment to working with the AbilityOne Program to market the product(s) solicited herein to Government customers. Preference is given to manufacturers who have a dedicated team for Federal Government sales and marketing. Be willing to work with the NPA, NIB, and AbilityOne to ensure that the price to the end-users is a fair and reasonable price. Manufacturers� submissions must demonstrate that proposed products meet the criteria listed above, as well as indicate what functions the nonprofit agency�s employees would perform. The deadline for response is 11/25/2026 The written, electronic responses should be directed to the contact listed in this Notice. Questions should be directed by email to jwhite@@nib.org. The subject line should begin with �Question: Sources Sought CP- CP-10-27-2026-01 Door Hardware Information regarding the Commission can be found at www.abilityone.gov. Select Operation Memoranda, then select Memorandum Number 22.

title: Request for Information (RFI) for Aerial Targets Branch (EBAY) Air Force Aerial Target Solutions
description: Issued pursuant to Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) FAR 15.101(c) and RFO FAR Part 10 solely for information, market research, and planning purposes. This market survey is conducted by the Aerial Targets Program Office (AFLCMC/EBAY) under the Air Force Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Weapons (AFPAE/WP) to obtain industry capabilities, rough order of magnitude (ROM) information, and data needed to support commercial product/service, non-developmental item (NDI), and small business determinations under RFO FAR 10.001(f), and to inform acquisition planning. Per Title 10, U.S. Code �4172, major munitions and missile programs must demonstrate lethality against appropriate, threat-representative targets prior to full-rate production. The Aerial Targets mission is to provide target aircraft that replicate threat systems, including performance, signatures, and countermeasures of adversary aircraft. The objective of this RFI is to identify a range of solutions to populate a family for systems needed throughout the spectrum of missions in Defensive and Offensive Counter Air capabilities. These solutions may represent the full range of airborne threats, spanning from inexpensive �hobby drones� to the most advance adversary fighter and large-scale aircraft. This RFI is intended to: Identify commercially available or near-term solutions Understand industry capabilities and innovative approaches Inform future acquisition strategies and budgetary requirements and assist the agency in making commerciality, NDI, and small business set-aside determinations See attached RFI and Question and Answer documents and for additional details. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ In accordance with Section 10 of the attached RFI, attached are the final Questions and Answers posted on 11 SEPTEMBER 2026. ALL FINAL RESPONSES ARE DUE BY 28 SEPTEMBER 2026 @ 1600 CENTRAL.

title: Armored Transport Services
description: This announcement constitutes a Notice of Proposed Contract Action. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation. The Bureau of Engraving and Printing (BEP) intends to establish a non-personal services blanket purchase agreement (BPA) for Armored Car Services. title: Infantry Squad Vehicle Follow-On Market Questionnaire
description: The United States Army is seeking information to identify qualified and capable industry partners to support the continued development, production, and sustainment of the Infantry Squad family of vehicles. This critical initiative focuses on assessing the industrial base's capacity to deliver and support two primary commercial platforms: the Infantry Squad Vehicle 9-Passenger (ISV-9) and the Infantry Squad Vehicle Utility (ISV-Utility). This request for information (RFI) does not constitute a request for proposals; submission of any information in response to this market survey is purely voluntary; the government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred.

title: Fire Truck Maintenance & Repair
description: COMBINED SYNOPSIS / SOLICITATION FOR COMMERCIAL SERVICES Solicitation Number: PANROC-26-P-0000 034092 Issuing Activity: Army Contracting Command � Rock Island (ACC-RI), Rock Island Arsenal, IL Requirement Title: Fire Department Fire Apparatus Maintenance and Repair Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) Notice Type: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation (Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source Blanket Purchase Agreement) Authority: FAR Subpart 12.6, FAR Part 13 (FAR 13.303 and FAR 13.106-1(b)) SECTION 1: GENERAL INFORMATION AND SYNOPSIS DESCRIPTION Overview & Authority: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 12.6, Streamlined Procedures for Evaluation and Solicitation for Commercial Products and Commercial Services, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation Type: This acquisition is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ). The Government intends to establish a single Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) utilizing Simplified Acquisition Procedures pursuant to FAR Part 13. Regulatory Provisions and Clauses: The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2024-05 and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) publication current as of the solicitation issuance date. NAICS Code, Size Standard, and Competition: NAICS Code: 811118 Small Business Size Standard: $9.0 Million Product Service Code (PSC): J023 Competition / Sole Source Authority: This requirement is being solicited as a sole-source action to Legacy Fire Apparatus under the authority of FAR 6.302-1, Soliciting from a Single Source. Market research demonstrated that Legacy Fire Apparatus is the only responsible vendor within the geographic vicinity capable of providing Emergency Vehicle Technicians (EVT) meeting the mandatory 40-minute emergency response time requirement for the Rock Island Arsenal (RIA) Fire Department. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. SECTION 2: CONTRACT LINE ITEM NUMBERS (CLINs) & PRICING SCHEDULE The contractor shall provide all management, tools, equipment, labor, and parts necessary to perform maintenance, diagnostics, and repairs on RIA fire apparatuses. Pricing under the resulting BPA will be established based on fixed hourly labor rates and part markup percentages for the 5-year ordering period. Period of Performance: 01 December 2026 through 30 November 2031 CLIN Description Estimated Qty Unit Unit Price Total Est. Amount 0001 Standard Hourly Maintenance Labor Rate Standard business hours (Monday�Friday). Work performed in accordance with SOW and applicable NFPA standards. 500 HR $__________ $__________ 0002 Overtime / Emergency Hourly Labor Rate After-hours, weekends, and federal holidays. Work performed with a mandatory on-site response time of 40 minutes. (Guaranteed 2-hour minimum per service call). 250 HR $__________ $__________ 0003 Scheduled Annual NFPA Inspections & Certifications Annual inspection/testing for 3 apparatuses per NFPA 1911/1914. 5 YR $__________ $__________ 0004 Replacement Parts & Materials Direct replacement parts/components provided at vendor catalog/cost plus fixed markup percentage of NTE 10% (Material Pass-Through). Estimated Cost Ceiling. 1 LOT NTE $75,000 NTE $75,000.00 Note: Quantities above are non-binding estimates used for price evaluation purposes only and is an estimate over the course of 5 years. Individual Call Orders will establish actual requirements and firm-fixed-price amounts. SECTION 3: STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) 1. Purpose Maintenance and repair of the Rock Island Arsenal Fire Apparatuses in support of the Rock Island Arsenal Fire and Emergency Services Division, Force Protection, located at Rock Island Arsenal (RIA), Rock Island, IL. 2. Scope & Technical Requirements The contractor shall utilize Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) parts unless otherwise approved in writing by the Ordering Officer or when OEM parts are unavailable within a critical operational timeframe. 2.1. Applicable NFPA Standards: Maintenance service for emergency vehicles and equipment shall be performed according to related National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) standards, including but not limited to: NFPA 1500: Standard on Fire Department Occupational Safety, Health, and Wellness Program NFPA 1071: Standard for Emergency Vehicle Technician Professional Qualifications (2006 Edition or most current) NFPA 1906: Standard for Wildland Fire Apparatus NFPA 1911: Standard for the Inspection, Maintenance, Testing, and Retirement of In-Service Emergency Vehicles NFPA 1914: Standard for Testing Fire Department Aerial Devices These standards will be used as a mandatory guide for inspections, repairs, and maintenance practices, and to establish an emergency vehicle service frequency program. The Contractor�s technicians shall meet or exceed NFPA 1071 certification qualifications. Certifications from the Contractor�s technicians must be delivered to the Contracting Officer in .pdf format no more than fourteen (14) days after completion. Certifications may be delivered via electronic mail. 2.2. Emergency Response & On-Call Requirement: The Contractor shall provide an updated on-call list of qualified Legacy Fire technicians (with active telephone numbers) to authorized Government Purchase Card (GPC) cardholders/Ordering Officers for after-hours emergency repair support. 40-Minute Response Time: When repairs are required, the qualified Emergency Vehicle Technician on the call list must report to the Rock Island Arsenal maintenance shop within forty (40) minutes of telephonic notification per RIA Fire Department policy. 3. Equipment Inventory (Covered Vehicles) The make, model, and inventory of emergency response apparatuses to be maintained and repaired under this agreement include: Vehicle ID # Manufacturer Model Year Equipment Type E-41-2 Pierce 2022 Pumper / Engine E-42 Emergency One (E-One) 2016 Pumper / Engine T-41 Pierce 2011 Truck / Aerial 4. Period of Performance The ordering period shall extend five, one-year Ordering Periods from 01 December 2026 through 30 November 2031. 5. Terms of the Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) & Ordering Procedures 5.1. BPA Instrument: This requirement is established as a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) under FAR 13.303. The Government Purchase Card (GPC) will serve as the exclusive method of ordering and payment for services and parts. The BPA is managed by Army Sustainment Command (ASC), 404th Army Field Support Brigade (AFSB), Logistics Readiness Center (LRC) (ASDL-COP). 5.2. Financial and Call Limitations: Individual Call Limit: The maximum BPA Call Limit per transaction shall not exceed $25,000.00. Work estimated to exceed $25,000.00 shall be routed to the Contracting Officer at Army Contracting Command-Rock Island for alternative procurement action. Master Agreement Dollar Limit: The cumulative BPA Master Dollar Limit for the entire period of performance (01-Dec-2026 to 30-Nov-2031) is $273,335.00. STRICT LIMITATION: There are NO exceptions to these dollar limitations. 5.3. Authorized Purchasers / Ordering Officers: Only individuals specifically designated by the Contracting Officer in writing are authorized to issue calls and obligate funds under this agreement. title: NLS DTBM Breath Switch
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation in accordance with FAR Part 13. This is a simplified acquisition to establish a contract for a breath switch. This breath switch will be used to control the Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) DS-1 (Digital Standard version 1), DA-1 (Digital Advanced player version 1), and DA-2 (Digital Advanced player version 2) allowing for control of the device using pulses of air. The contractor shall develop both a breath switch and a Technical Data Package upon which this device is based. The breath switch shall consist of a micro controller and associated circuitry, a USB-A connector, housing, and a mouth tube. A full description of breath switch requirements is contained in Attachment J-3. The breath switch�s tubing shall be food safe (i.e., silicone). The contractor shall develop any required tooling, production/test equipment, and procedures required to manufacture the breath switch. This work shall comprise two phases: (1) a non-recurring engineering (NRE) phase and (2) a full-production phase. This is intended to be a single-award 5-year IDIQ above the simplified acquisition threshold. Please see the attached solicitation and associated attachments for more details.

title: Fællesudbud af trykkeriydelser (2027)
description: Fællesudbud for Københavns Kommune og Frederiksberg Kommune om indgåelse af to rammeaftaler på trykkeriydelser, en rammeaftale for hver kommune. Rammeaftalerne har en løbetid på 4 år og omfatter bestilling, produktion og levering af tryksager, herunder bl.a. plakater, foldere, hæfter, visitkort, bykort og kopi-print. Tilbudsgiver afgiver et samlet tilbud på udbuddets to rammeaftaler, vindende Tilbudsgiver tildeles begge rammeaftaler.Ordregivers krav til kontraktvilkår fremgår af rammeaftale udkastet (bilag A), mens kravene til ydelserne er detaljeret beskrevet i den tekniske specifikation (bilag 1).Københavns Kommune er udførende Ordregiver på udbuddet.

title: Modtagelse og behandling af farligt emballeret affald. Indsamling, håndtering og afsætning af trykflasker.
description: Udbuddet vedrører ydelser i forbindelse med håndtering af farligt affald, herunder modtagelse, håndtering, afsætning, indsamling og transport af farligt affald samt levering af emballage og øvrige materialer til håndteringen. Der er tre delaftaler hvor tilbudsgivere kan byde på én, to eller alle delaftaler. • Delaftale 1: Emballeret farligt affald samt køb og leje af emballage til farligt affald • Delaftale 2: Indsamling, håndtering og afsætning af trykflasker • Delaftale 3 – Indsamling, håndtering og behandling af farlig maling UN1263 og gråzoneaffald Ydelserne leveres til samtlige ordregivers genbrugspladser, samt mindre erhvervsvirksomheder i ordregivers ejerkommuner medmindre andet fremgår af Aftalen. De konkrete ydelser varierer mellem de enkelte delaftaler. For nærmere beskrivelse af de udbudte ydelser, herunder de krav ydelserne skal opfylde, henvises til udbudsmaterialet kravspecifikationen (bilag 2) og tilbudslisten (Bilag 3.1-3), samt eventuelle rettelser og besvarelse af spørgsmål (bilag 1).
